Fed voices are now visibly split heading into the Sep 15-16 FOMC: Williams (dovish) vs. Goolsbee/Hammack (hawkish, want more hikes) -- Waller speaks today 20:30 SGT and Friday's NFP (cons 55K vs -23K prior) is the pivotal print. Gaps this run: no fresh Sep 2-3 company-specific catalysts found for HK tech (Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC) or SGX names (DBS/OCBC/Singtel/REITs) beyond the broad index-level moves -- flagged rather than padded with stale items.

items.headline: ADP August print misses hard at +38K vs ~47K consensus, weakest since January -- drives Wednesday's relief rally
items.summary: ADP/Stanford Digital Economy Lab reported private-sector payrolls rose just 38,000 in August, well below consensus and July's upwardly-revised 46K. Manufacturing (-17K), professional services (-16K) and information (-4K) shed jobs, offset only by education/health (+45K) and leisure/hospitality (+16K). ADP's chief economist flagged four years of decelerating pay growth.
items.actionable: Reduced Sept-hike odds drove Wednesday's broad rally and the silver/gold miner spike (SILJ +5.36%, HL +8.69%) -- Friday's NFP (cons 55K vs -23K prior) is now the pivotal print for whether this dovish repricing holds.

items.headline: US strikes Iranian government tankers directly for the first time under new 'tanker-for-tanker' policy -- Hormuz conflict escalates further, not cools
items.summary: The US conducted a large strike wave (~100 targets) against IRGC air-defense, radar, mine-laying and drone-launch sites, and for the first time struck two Iranian government tankers directly under a Trump-approved deterrence policy. Iran's foreign ministry alleges a separate US strike hit a wedding in Kuhestak (50+ claimed casualties, unverified); Jordan intercepted 10 of 13 Iranian ballistic missiles and Bahrain intercepted drones. A US official told Axios the tanker strikes 'bought at least a month' of reduced shipping-attack risk.
items.actionable: Do not read Wednesday's equity calm as resolution -- this is a live escalation (first direct tanker strikes, a civilian-casualty controversy) that could reprice risk assets overnight on any single fresh headline; crypto already sold off specifically on this news even as equities rallied on jobs data.

items.headline: Fed voices split heading into Sep 15-16 FOMC: Williams pushes back on 'inevitable' hike, Goolsbee/Hammack want more tightening
items.summary: NY Fed's Williams said there is 'no clear science right now' on whether policy needs to tighten further and that inflation is 'moving slowly down' as tariff effects fade. The same day, Chicago Fed's Goolsbee warned the economy is 'inching toward dangers of overheat' on AI-driven demand with inflation progress having 'stalled out,' while Cleveland Fed's Hammack said she expects more than one further hike is needed against 'broadening inflation.'
items.actionable: A genuinely divided committee -- watch Waller's remarks today (20:30 SGT) and Friday's NFP to see which camp gains the upper hand before the Sep 15-16 decision; size any duration or gold/miner additions with this binary in mind.

items.headline: CLARITY Act Senate passage odds collapse to under 20% from a 58% high ahead of Sep 15 cloture vote
items.summary: Polymarket's implied odds of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act passing have fallen from a 58% high to below 20% ahead of the scheduled Sep 15 Senate floor-debate cloture vote. Failure would leave crypto regulated by enforcement rather than statute until at least 2029; one analyst projects a 10-25% BTC correction risk on failure.
items.actionable: A genuine binary tail-risk event for the crypto sleeve, not a formality -- worth explicitly sizing or hedging into the Sep 15 vote given how far the passage odds have deteriorated since May's committee approval.

items.headline: RBNZ hikes to 2.75%, Bank of Canada holds at 2.25% and explicitly flags Hormuz oil prices as an inflation risk
items.summary: RBNZ delivered a widely-expected 25bp hike to 2.75%, flagging one more possible hike this year with inflation running 4.1%, driven partly by Middle-East-linked fuel prices. The Bank of Canada held at 2.25% as expected, with its statement explicitly citing 'the longer high oil prices and elevated refinery margins persist, the greater the risk of spillover' alongside US tariff/counter-tariff risk.
items.actionable: Both decisions were priced in and non-events for markets, but confirm G7 central banks now treat the Hormuz conflict as a structural inflation input rather than a transient shock -- a read-through for how the Fed may frame oil-driven inflation at the Sep 15-16 meeting.

items.headline: Berkshire's Abel gives fullest public rationale yet for the ~83% Alphabet stake build: 'we saw Google as a significant player' in AI
items.summary: On CNBC's Squawk Box, Berkshire CEO Greg Abel detailed the reasoning behind Q2's ~$37B, ~106M-share Alphabet stake (now Berkshire's #3 holding behind Apple and Amex): visibility from within Berkshire's own operating companies on how they use AI convinced the team Google was a 'significant player.' Buffett, now Chairman, said 'I initiated it, but Abel is the decider.'
items.actionable: New attribution color on an already-known Q2 13F position -- reinforces conviction rather than signaling a new trade, but useful for the whale-consensus narrative on GOOGL already flagged as the portfolio's broadest multi-investor signal.

items.headline: Gold-miners index posts best August since 1994, +33% vs. bullion's smaller gain, as the sector's structural bull run continues
items.summary: The NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index rose roughly 33% in August, more than 3x bullion's own gain, before Tuesday's hawkish-Fed-driven pullback and Wednesday's sharp rebound (already reflected in the price spine: GDX +3.13%, SILJ +5.36%, HL +8.69%, AG +6.75% on Wed).
items.actionable: The miners complex remains in a powerful structural uptrend on safe-haven and inflation-hedge demand tied to the live Iran conflict -- treat Wednesday's sharp single-day pops as a continuation of this trend, not a one-off bounce, while staying mindful of the sleeve's high beta to Fed-hike repricing.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export curbs on MP Materials and USA Rare Earth remain paused through Nov 10 2026
items.summary: China added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export-control list in June 2026 as part of its toughest-yet magnet/rare-earth curbs; those controls are currently suspended, with the pause set to expire 10 November 2026. Separately, Lynas (largest non-China refiner) posted record FY26 revenue (+76% to A$977.9m) on record non-China pricing despite a profit miss on rising costs.
items.actionable: A dated fuse worth calendaring for the rare-earths sleeve -- if the pause is not extended, expect a fresh re-rating catalyst for the ex-China basket (MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels/USA Rare Earth) heading into mid-November.

items.headline: Singapore's STI falls 0.8% to 5,710 ahead of Wall Street's rebound -- catch-up watch into today's open
items.summary: The Straits Times Index fell nearly 1% Tuesday as the oil-driven Hormuz escalation hit regional sentiment, lagging what would become Wednesday's sharp US relief rally. No SGX-specific company catalysts (DBS/OCBC/Singtel/REITs) were found dated Sep 1-3 beyond this broad index-level move.
items.actionable: SGX has not yet had a session to react to Wednesday's US rebound (opens 09:00 SGT today) -- watch for a catch-up bounce in the banks/REITs sleeve at today's open.
